(182)

Let us denote with
\tilde{V}_{\textup{post}}
the set of post-selection vertices of
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
.

Then, we define a teleportation causal model on
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
through
definition

8
. In particular, this construction prescribes that the same maps and Hilbert spaces are associated to vertices and edges that are preserved from
G
to
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
. To pre- and post-selection vertices we associate (without loss of generality,
corollary

16
) Bell teleportation protocols (
definition

5
), i.e., for all
v\in V_{\textsc{s}}(G_{c,\textsc{tp}})
and
e=(v,v^{\prime})\in\mathrm{Out}(v)
we associate to the corresponding pre-selection vertex
R_{v}^{e}
the Bell state

\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}=|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{Out}(R_{v}^{e})}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}_{v}|}\sum_{x,y\in\mathcal{X}_{v}}|x\rangle\langle y|_{(R_{v}^{e},T_{v}^{e})}\otimes|x\rangle\langle y|_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}

(183)

and to the corresponding post-selection vertex
T_{v}^{e}
and outcome
t=\checkmark
the CP map acting on all
\rho\in\mathcal{L}\left(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{In}(T_{v}^{e})}\right)\cong\mathcal{L}\left(\mathcal{H}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{(R_{v}^{e},T_{v}^{e})}\right)
as

\begin{split}\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}(\rho)&=\mathrm{Tr}\left(|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{In}(T_{v}^{e})}\rho\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}_{v}|}\mathrm{Tr}\left[\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{v}}\left(|x\rangle\langle y|_{\mathcal{H}_{(v,T^{e}_{v})}}\otimes|x\rangle\langle y|_{\mathcal{H}_{(R^{e}_{v},T^{e}_{v})}}\right)\rho\right].\end{split}

(184)

By
definition

12
, given an observed event
x:=\{x_{v}\in\mathcal{X}_{v}\}_{v\in V}
, the probability of
\mathsf{Cm}_{G}
(see
Step 4
) is defined as

\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x)_{G}=\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}\left(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=\checkmark\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in\tilde{V}_{\textup{post}}}\right)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}},

(185)

where
\tilde{V}_{\textup{post}}
denotes the set of post-selection vertices of
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
.

Step 6:

Finally, we show that the causal models
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
(introduced in
Step 3
) and
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
(introduced in
Step 5
) are equivalent, in the sense that for all observed events
x:=\{x_{v}\in\mathcal{X}_{v}\}_{v\in V}
it holds

\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}\left(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=\checkmark\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in\tilde{V}_{\textup{post}}}\right)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}=\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=1\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{\prime}})_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}.

(186)

Firstly, we notice that the construction of
G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}
and
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
give the same causal graphs, indeed, the subsequent substitutions in
equation

172
and
equation

174
are equivalent to
equation

182
. Let us show that the maps associated to each vertex are equivalent in the two causal models,
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
and
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
. We have:

1.

For all vertices which are preserved from
G
to
G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}
(and
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
),
v\in V
the maps associated in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
and
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
are equal (see
equations

176
and
180
), i.e., for all
\rho\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{In}(v)})
it holds

\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{v}(\rho)=\mathcal{M}_{x}^{v}(\rho)

(187)

where we recall that
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{v}
is the map associated to
v
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
and
\mathcal{M}_{x}^{v}
is the map associated to
v
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
.

2.

For all post-selection vertices, i.e., for all
v\in V_{\textsc{s}}(G_{c,\textsc{tp}})
and
e\in\mathrm{Out}(v)
, we have (by the decoherence condition for observed vertices in
definition

2
)

\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}\circ\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{v}=\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}\circ\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}\circ\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{v}

(188)

where all maps
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}
are in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
and
\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}
is a decohering channel acting as
\mathcal{D}_{e}(\rho)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{e}}|x\rangle\langle x|\rho|x\rangle\langle x|
for any
\rho\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{e})
.
In order to evaluate probabilities, the maps of
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
are composed as described in
definition

3
. In particular, the map
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}
is always composed with
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x}^{v}
as in
equation

188
, hence, it can be replaced with
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}\circ\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}
without affecting probabilities. Thus, we have for all
\rho\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{In}(T_{v}^{e})})

\begin{split}\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}\circ\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}(\rho)=&\mathrm{Tr}\left(|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{In}(T_{v}^{e})}\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}(\rho)\right)\\
\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textup{\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{lem:trace and decoherence}}}}{{=}}&\mathrm{Tr}\left[\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}\left(|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{In}(T_{v}^{e})}\right)\rho\right]\end{split}

(189)

and

\begin{split}\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}\left(|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{In}(T^{e}_{v})}\right)&=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}_{v}|}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{v}}|x\rangle\langle x|_{{(v,T_{v}^{e})}}\otimes|x\rangle\langle x|_{(R_{v}^{e},T_{v}^{e})}.\end{split}

(190)

Thus we can compare this map, associated to the post-selection vertex
T^{e}_{v}
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
, to the map
\mathcal{M}_{1}^{T_{v}^{e}}
associated to the same post-selection vertex in
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
(see
equation

177
). It holds

\tilde{\mathcal{M}}^{T_{v}^{e}}_{\checkmark}\circ\mathcal{D}_{(v,T_{v}^{e})}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}_{v}|}\mathcal{M}_{1}^{T_{v}^{e}}.

(191)

3.

For all pre-selection vertices, i.e., for all
v\in V_{\textsc{s}}(G_{c,\textsc{tp}})
and
e=(v,v^{\prime})\in\mathrm{Out}(v)
we have

\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x^{\prime}}^{v^{\prime}}\circ\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textup{\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{lem: decoherence in fcm}}}}{{=}}\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x^{\prime}}^{v^{\prime}}\circ\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}\circ\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}

(192)

where
\tilde{}
denotes associations in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
and
\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}
is a decohering channel. In order to evaluate probabilities, the maps of
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
are composed as described in
definition

3
. In particular, the state
\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}
is always composed with the map
\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_{x^{\prime}}^{v^{\prime}}
as in
eq.

192
, hence, the state
\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}
can be replaced with
\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}\circ\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}
without affecting probabilities. Thus, we can compare the decohered state
\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}\circ\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}
, associated to the pre-selection vertex
R_{v}^{e}
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
, to the state
\sigma^{R_{v}^{e}}
associated to the same pre-selection vertex in
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
(see
equation

178
). It holds:

\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}\circ\tilde{\sigma}^{R_{v}^{e}}=\mathcal{D}_{(R_{v}^{e},v^{\prime})}\left(|\Phi^{+}\rangle\langle\Phi^{+}|_{\mathrm{Out}(R_{v}^{e})}\right)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textup{\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{eq:decohered_bellstate_new}}}}{{=}}\sigma^{R_{v}^{e}}.

(193)

Using the probability rule in
definition

3
, we can easily see that the conditional probabilities in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
and
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
satisfy

\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}\left(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=\checkmark\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in\tilde{V}_{\text{post}}}\right)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}=\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=1\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{\prime}})_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}},

(194)

notice that the scaling factor between the two maps in
equation

191
drops out once we condition on successful post-selections.

Finally, we can combine the results of
Steps 1-6
to complete the proof. Indeed, we have

\begin{split}\hyperlink{probf}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{\mathrm{f}}}(x)_{G}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textbf{S1}}}{{=}}&\hyperlink{probfacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{f,acyc}}}}\left(x|\{t_{v}=1\}_{T_{v}\in V_{\textup{post}}}\right)_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}}\\
\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textbf{S2}}}{{=}}&\hyperlink{probfacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{f,acyc}}}}(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=1\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{\prime}})_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}\\
\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textbf{S3}}}{{=}}&\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}(x,\{t^{e}_{v}=1\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{\prime}})_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}\\
\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textbf{S6}}}{{=}}&\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}\left(x|\{t^{e}_{v}=\checkmark\}_{T^{e}_{v}\in\tilde{V}_{\text{post}}}\right)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}\\
\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textbf{S5}}}{{=}}&\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}\left(x\right)_{G}\\
\end{split}

(195)

where
\hyperlink{probf}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{\mathrm{f}}}_{G}
is the probability in
\mathsf{fCm}_{G}
(
Step 0
),
\hyperlink{probfacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{f,acyc}}}}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}}
in
\mathsf{fCm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}}
(
Step 1
),
\hyperlink{probfacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{f,acyc}}}}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
in
\mathsf{fCm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
(
Step 2
),
\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{G_{c,\textsc{tp}}^{\prime}}
(
Step 3
),
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{G}
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{G}
(
Step 4
) and
\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
in
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
(
Step 5
).

∎

Appendix D
Proofs of
section

4

See
[use
cref
not
ref
]

Proof.

In the first step of
definition

6
, the graph
G^{\prime}
is acyclic.
The second step introduces pre- and post-selection vertices,
R_{i}
and
T_{i}
, and associated edges according to
equation

47
.
To show that this step preserves acyclicity, notice that a directed graph is acyclic if and only if it can be drawn on a page with all directed edges oriented from bottom to top of the page
26
26

26

This representation is equivalent to a Hasse diagram for partially ordered sets, recognising the fact that every directed acyclic graph induces a partial order and vice versa.
.
Since
G^{\prime}
is acyclic, we can represent it on a page through such a diagram.
We now add the pre- and post-selection vertices to this diagram by drawing all the
R_{i}
at the bottom of the page, below all other vertices, and all the
T_{i}
at the top of the page, above all the other vertices.
Since all pre-selection vertices
R_{i}
only have outgoing edges and all post-selection vertices
T_{i}
only have incoming arrows, both of which will be oriented from bottom to top in our diagram, it follows that
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
is acyclic.
∎

See
[use
cref
not
ref
]

Proof.

Proof in a special case.

Consider the special case where
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
and
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}
were constructed by choosing

\displaystyle E_{\textsc{s}}({G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2})=E_{\textsc{s}}({G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1})\cup\{e_{0}\},

(196)

i.e.,
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}
splits the same edges as
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
plus the edge
e_{0}
. Let
V_{\textup{post}}^{1}
denote the set of post-selection vertices of
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
and
t:=\{t_{i}\in\{\text{✓},\text{✗}\}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{1}}
. Then, taking
t_{0}
to be the outcome of the post-selection vertex associated to the edge
e_{0}
, we have
t\cup t_{0}:=\{t_{i}\in\{\text{✓},\text{✗}\}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{2}}
.

Consider the probability
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}
associated to the causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}
on the causal graph underlying the teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
. As this is an acyclic causal model by construction (c.f.,
lemma

7
), this probability is immediately given by applying the acyclic probability rule of
definition

3
to this causal model. Here,
x=\{x_{v}\in\mathcal{X}_{v}\}_{v\in V_{\textup{o}}}
denotes an observed event on
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
(which is also an event on
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}
, since these graphs have the same observed vertices). We can write

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}=\mathrm{Tr}[F^{(x,t)}\rho^{(x,t)}],

(197)

where we defined the subnormalized density matrix and POVM element
\rho^{(x,t)},F^{(x,t)}\in\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{H}_{e_{0}})
obtained from composing all the channels of the causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}
, but leaving the composition along the
e_{0}
edge as the last step.
27
27

27

This decomposition is not unique for teleportation graphs with disconnected components, in which case we can pick any such decomposition.

We then consider the post-selected teleportation protocol that the causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
implements in place of the edge
e_{0}=:(v_{0},v_{0}^{\prime})
, with associated pre- and post-selection vertices
R_{0}
and
T_{0}
.
The associated teleportation probability is denoted
p_{\textsc{tp}}\in(0,1]
.
For convenience, we label as
A
,
B
and
C
the Hilbert spaces involve in this teleportation protocol:

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{A}=\mathcal{H}_{(v_{0},T_{0})},\qquad\mathcal{H}_{B}=\mathcal{H}_{(R_{0},T_{0})},\qquad\mathcal{H}_{C}=\mathcal{H}_{(R_{0},v_{0}^{\prime})}.

(198)

This allows us to denote the post-selected teleportation implementation as
({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB},{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})
.

Thanks to the Hilbert space identities of
equation

49
, we have
\mathcal{H}_{e_{0}}=\mathcal{H}_{A}=\mathcal{H}_{C}
.
We can thus rewrite
equation

197
as

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}

\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}_{A}[F^{(x,t)}_{A}\rho^{(x,t)}_{A}]

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{p_{\textsc{tp}}}\mathrm{Tr}_{AB}\left[({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB}\otimes F^{(x,t)}_{C})(\rho^{(x,t)}_{A}\otimes{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})\right]

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{p_{\textsc{tp}}}\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t,t_{0}=\text{✓})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}},

(199)

where
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t,t_{0})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
denotes the probabilities associated to the causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
on the causal graph underlying the teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}
.
In the last equation, we used that
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}
and
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
can be chosen to have the same associated
\rho^{(x,t)}
and
F^{(x,t)}
(to see this, one may for simplicity restrict all the post-selected teleportation protocols to be implemented as in
definition

5
— if we establish
proposition

10
in this case, the general result follows from
corollary

16
).
We can now relate the success probability
p_{\checkmark}^{(i)}
of the causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,i}}
on the teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,i}
for
i\in\{1,2\}
.
By
definition

9
, we have

\displaystyle p_{\checkmark}^{(1)}

\displaystyle=\sum_{x}\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t=\text{✓})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}

(200)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{p_{\textsc{tp}}}\sum_{x}\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t=\text{✓},t_{0}=\text{✓})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}

(201)

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{p_{\textsc{tp}}}p_{\checkmark}^{(2)},

(202)

where the sum
\sum_{x}
runs over all
x=\{x_{v}\in\mathcal{X}_{v}\}_{v\in V_{\textup{o}}}
, and where we denote with
t=\text{✓}
the event
\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}^{1}}
.
We see that the two success probabilities differ by a multiplicative constant (the success probability
p_{\textsc{tp}}
of the post-selected teleportation protocol defined by
\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
for the split edge
e_{0}
), and hence,
p_{\checkmark}^{(1)}
is zero if and only if
p_{\checkmark}^{(2)}
is zero.
Hence, the probabilities
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}
are defined if and only if the probabilities
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}
are defined.
Furthermore, if they are defined, we can relate them as follows (again appealing to
definition

9
):

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}

\displaystyle=\frac{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t=\text{✓})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}}}{p_{\checkmark}^{(1)}}=\frac{p_{\textsc{tp}}}{p_{\textsc{tp}}}\frac{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,t=\text{✓},t_{0}=\text{✓})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}}}{p_{\checkmark}^{(2)}}=\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x)_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}},

(203)

which completes the proof in this case.

Proof in the general case.

Consider two general elements of
\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
,
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1},{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}\in\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
.
We can prove the general statement by first noticing that the repeated application of the above argument can be used to prove that the probabilities of both
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,1}
and
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,2}
are equivalent to those of
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,0}
, where the latter corresponds to the graph where all the edges have been split (i.e.,
E_{\textsc{s}}({G_{\textsc{tp}}}_{,0})=E
, where
G=(V,E)
).
The result follows by transitivity.
∎

Proof.

We start by considering a teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}\in\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
associated with our given graph
G
, and the causal model
{\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}}
on the teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
, associated with a set
V_{\textup{post}}:=\{T_{i}\}_{i=1}^{k}
of post-selection vertices.

The associated probability distribution
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
is then given by
definition

3
since
{\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}}
is an acyclic causal model by construction (as
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
is a directed acyclic graph,
lemma

7
).

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}=\mathrm{Tr}\left[\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}^{(i)}\,\mathcal{C}_{x}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}^{(i)}\right)\right],

(204)

where the state
\bigotimes_{i}{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}^{(i)}
acts on
\bigotimes_{i}\mathcal{H}_{(R_{i},T_{i})}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}^{\prime}}
, and consists of the tensor product of the pre-selection states of each post-selected teleportation protocol.
The POVM element
\bigotimes{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}^{(i)}
acts on
\bigotimes_{i}\mathcal{H}_{(R_{i},T_{i})}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}}
and consists of the tensor product of the post-selection POVM elements of each post-selected teleportation protocol.
Recall that the map
\mathcal{C}_{x}
takes inputs in
\mathcal{L}(\bigotimes_{i}\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}^{\prime}})
and outputs in
\mathcal{L}(\bigotimes_{i}\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}})
.
Let us define the following Hilbert spaces:

\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{A}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}},\qquad\mathcal{H}_{B}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}\mathcal{H}_{(R_{i},T_{i})},\qquad\mathcal{H}_{C}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}^{\prime}}.

(205)

By construction (
definition

8
), we have that
\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}}=\mathcal{H}_{e_{i}^{\prime}}
, so that we also have
\mathcal{H}_{A}=\mathcal{H}_{C}
.
We denote
{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}^{(i)}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{k}{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}^{(i)}
, and we denote the map
\mathcal{C}_{x}
as
(\mathcal{C}_{x})_{A|C}
.
The probabilities of
equation

204
can be rewritten as

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}=\mathrm{Tr}_{AB}[{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB}(\mathcal{C}_{x})_{A|C}({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})].

(206)

It is easy to prove that
({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB},{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})
implements a post-selected teleportation protocol.
Indeed, this follows from the linearity of the post-selected teleportation condition
equation

45
, which allows to successfully teleport part of a multipartite state (see also
lemma

25
), together with the fact that
({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB},{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})
corresponds to
k
parallel independent post-selected teleportation protocols.
Furthermore, it is easy to see that the teleportation success probability of
({\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}E}_{AB},{\color[rgb]{0.7891,0.0781,0.1133}\varphi}_{BC})
is the product of the individual teleportation probabilities.
Using
lemma

28
, we see that the probabilities of
equation

206
can be rewritten as

\displaystyle\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}=\left(\prod_{i=1}^{k}p_{\textsc{tp}}^{(i)}\right)\mathrm{cycle}(\mathcal{C}_{x}).

(207)

Finally, by recalling
definition

9
of the post-selection success probability
p_{\checkmark}
and
definition

12
of the probability
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x)_{G}
of the observed outcomes of the original causal model
\mathsf{Cm}_{G}
in terms of the probability
\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}(x,\{t_{i}=\text{✓}\}_{T_{i}\in V_{\textup{post}}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
of the teleportation causal model
{\mathsf{Cm}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}}
(on the graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
), we see that
equation

207
immediately implies the required
equation

57
,
∎

Proof.

(Soundness)

From
definition

21
, we have
(V_{1}\perp^{p}V_{2}|V_{3})_{G}\Leftrightarrow\exists{G_{\textsc{tp}}}\in\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
, such that
(V_{1}\perp^{d}V_{2}|V_{3}\cup V_{\textup{post}})_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}
, where
V_{\textup{post}}
is the set of all post-selection vertices in the chosen teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
. From
theorem

20
, it then follows that the conditional independence
(X_{1}\perp\!\!\!\perp X_{2}|X_{3}\cup V_{\textup{post}})_{\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}}
holds since
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}
is a directed acyclic graph (
lemma

7
). Finally, by
definition

12
, the probability distribution associated with a causal model on the possibly cyclic causal graph
G
is given by the corresponding probability computed in any representative teleportation graph
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}\in\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
with an additional conditioning on the associated post-selection vertices
V_{\textup{post}}
. Recall from
proposition

10
that this distribution is the same, independently of which representative
{G_{\textsc{tp}}}\in\mathbb{G}_{\textsc{tp}}(G)
is chosen. Therefore, using
definition

12
, we know that
(X_{1}\perp\!\!\!\perp X_{2}|X_{3}\cup V_{\textup{post}})_{\hyperlink{probacyc}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}{{}_{\mathrm{acyc}}}}_{{G_{\textsc{tp}}}}}
is equivalent to
(X_{1}\perp\!\!\!\perp X_{2}|X_{3})_{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{G}}
by
definition

21
, which completes the proof.

(Completeness)

Suppose we have a
p
-connection
(V_{1}\not\perp^{p}V_{2}|V_{3})_{G}
in the given directed graph
G
according to
definition

21
. Then by
lemma

40
this implies
p
-connection
(V_{1}\not\perp^{p,c}V_{2}|V_{3})_{G}
according to the alternative definition,
definition

39
, of this notion introduced in
[
FGV25
]
. By the completeness result for
\perp^{p,c}
proven in
[
FGV25
]
(Theorem 20)
28
28

28

We note that the notion of
definition

39
is referred to as
\perp^{p}
in
[
FGV25
]
, but we use
\perp^{p,c}
here to distinguish it from the
definition

21
introduced here.
, it follows that there exists a functional causal model (
definition

32
)
\mathsf{fCm}_{G}
on
G
where the conditional dependence
(X_{1}\not\perp\!\!\!\perp X_{2}|X_{3})_{\hyperlink{probf}{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{\mathrm{f}}}_{G}}
holds. By
lemma

37
,
\mathsf{fCm}_{G}
induces a causal model
\mathsf{Cm}(\mathsf{fCm})_{G}
on
G
with equivalent probabilities, and hence the same conditional dependence holds in this causal model of
G
,
(X_{1}\not\perp\!\!\!\perp X_{2}|X_{3})_{\hyperlink{prob}{\mathrm{Pr}}_{G}}
as required. This completes the proof.

∎
